name: Switzerland
tagline: The most expensive country in Europe and the one that most reliably justifies it.
summary: Switzerland is four language regions, twenty-six cantons and a public transport system that works so well it changes how you travel: a postbus meets the train, the train meets the boat, and all three are punctual to the minute. The Alps take up 60% of the land and are threaded with cable cars and mountain huts. Nothing is cheap and almost nothing is broken.

season.note: High mountain trails open from late June and close with the first snow in October. September is the best month up high: stable weather, clear air, cows coming down. May and November are between seasons and many lifts simply stop.

getting_around: The rail network is the product. A Swiss Travel Pass covers trains, buses, boats and most mountain railways; without one, individual tickets are eye-watering. Timetables interlock, so a four-minute connection is a real connection.
food: Cheese in its own right — Gruyère, Appenzeller, raclette scraped off the wheel
Rösti, and the Röstigraben that divides German from French Switzerland
Chocolate, bought from a maker rather than an airport

festivals.name: Fasnacht, Basel's carnival, starting at 4 am

know: Not in the EU; in Schengen. The franc is the currency and euros are accepted at a poor rate.
Mountain weather turns fast and huts must be booked; the SAC app carries conditions.
Tap water in villages and from most fountains is drinkable unless marked otherwise.

regions.name: The Bernese Oberland
regions.summary: The classic Alps: Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau above green valleys full of cog railways.

cities.name: Lauterbrunnen
cities.summary: A valley with vertical walls and seventy-two waterfalls, and car-free villages on the shelves above it.
highlights: Mürren and Gimmelwald, reachable only by cable car or on foot
Trümmelbach: ten glacier waterfalls inside the mountain
The Schilthorn, and the Eiger north face opposite

experiences.name: The North Face trail from Mürren
experiences.summary: Two hours on a balcony path with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau directly across the valley the whole way.

cities.name: Bern
cities.summary: The federal capital: six kilometres of arcades, a river you swim down, and Einstein's flat above a café.
highlights: Swimming the Aare with the current, as the city does all summer
Paul Klee's collection in a Renzo Piano wave

experiences.name: Float the Aare
experiences.summary: Walk upstream, get in, and let the river carry you back through the city — with a dry bag and a firm plan for getting out.

regions.name: Valais, Ticino & the South
regions.summary: The Matterhorn, the highest vineyards in Europe, and an Italian-speaking canton over the pass.

cities.name: Zermatt
cities.summary: A car-free village under the most photographed mountain on earth, with skiing possible in July.
highlights: The Matterhorn from the Riffelsee at sunrise, reflected
The Haute Route, ending here from Chamonix

cities.name: Lugano
cities.summary: Palm trees, a glacial lake and Italian spoken everywhere, twenty minutes from the Alps.
highlights: Monte Brè and Monte San Salvatore by funicular
The lakeside promenade and the ferries to Gandria
Italian food at Swiss standards of execution

regions.name: Graubünden & the East
regions.summary: Romansh country, the Rhaetian Railway's viaducts, and the highest mainline pass in the Alps.

cities.name: St. Moritz & the Engadin
cities.summary: A high valley of lakes at 1,800 metres, with sgraffito villages and 322 days of sun a year.
highlights: The Bernina Express over a UNESCO-listed railway to Italy
Segantini's paintings where he painted them
Cross-country skiing on frozen lakes in February

experiences.name: The Bernina line to Tirano
experiences.summary: From glacier to palm trees in four hours, over the Landwasser viaduct and around the Brusio spiral — booked as a normal train, not a tour.
